pulls.next_action: Wait for maintainer review and merge. Tags: v0.4.4 (post-merge, paired with PR #10's audit fixes).
pulls.notes:
Out-of-scope follow-up to the 2026-06-05 3-cycle audit (PR #10). Found two parallel data errors in verb_maps.rs:

1. Line 182: PAST_PARTICIPLE_TO_SIMPLE_PAST had ("shrunk", "shrunk") — a no-change self-map. Grammatically wrong: 'shrunk' is the PP, the simple past is 'shrank'. Flagged as out-of-scope finding #1 in the 2026-06-05 AUDIT.md.

2. Line 455: SIMPLE_PAST_TO_PRESENT had ("shrunk", "shrink") — but 'shrunk' is a PP, not a SP. The SP is 'shrank'. The original entry produced the right answer ("shrink") for the wrong reason (lookup of a PP form) and silently masked the missing 'shrank' entry. Discovered while doing fix #1 — parallel data error.

3. (Bonus) Stale header comments updated: 192/220 → 306/357 (verified by awk|grep -c). Self-review caught one I missed (line 348 in a third commit).

Pipeline round-trip after both fixes:
  shrunk (PP) → shrank (SP) → shrink (present)
  'The package was shrunk by the cold' → 'cold shrink package' (passive→active→present)
  'I shrank the package' → 'I shrink package' (past→present)

3 commits:
  b2c7671: fix(data): PP→SP "shrunk" → "shrank" (out-of-scope audit finding #1)
  6a795fb: fix(data): SP→PRES "shrunk" → "shrank" (parallel data error)

pulls.title: chore: gitignore uv.lock (per-machine artifact for libraries)
pulls.next_action: Trivial merge — single-line gitignore change with explanation comment. Will auto-merge once a maintainer reviews.
pulls.notes:
The 134-byte uv.lock was a leftover from a 2026-06-05 `uv run pytest` invocation during the audit session. Standard practice for Python libraries (not applications) is to gitignore uv.lock because:

- The editable install of rust-cave-001 produces a minimal lockfile that ties to the local Python version and absolute path of the checkout
- Committing it would create spurious churn for every contributor
- Library consumers don't benefit from this repo's lockfile (they have their own)

This is on a separate branch (chore/gitignore-uv-lock) to keep the main audit PR (#10) and the data-fix PR (#11) focused on their respective scopes. Per-claim atomicity beats bundling trivial changes with substantive ones.

1 commit:
  2e06d0c: chore: gitignore uv.lock (lockfile is per-machine for libraries)

pulls.next_action: Await review and merge into feature/platform-agnosticism. Once merged, rebase PR #8 onto updated base.
pulls.notes:
3 pre-existing config bugs fixed:
- BUG-1: obscura YAML block silently dropped (PartialAppConfig parsed it but load_config() never called merge_obscura).
- BUG-2: fingerprint block missing from PartialAppConfig entirely.
- BUG-3 (caught by new test): duplicate FingerprintConfig structs with mismatched serde defaults for sidecar_mode (config:: uses #[serde(default)] giving '', fingerprint:: uses #[serde(default = 'default_sidecar_mode')] giving 'http'). Engine copies fields between them, so omitted sidecar_mode in YAML silently produced empty runtime sidecar mode. Fixed by adding default_fingerprint_sidecar_mode() in config/mod.rs and a cross-reference comment.

pulls.next_action: MERGED into master at 2026-06-08T06:10:56Z (squash commit 5d20c16f). PR branch deleted. Local fix/env-lock-deduplication branch deleted. Master HEAD = 5d20c16f. 55/55 lib tests pass locally. Post-merge CI run 27119401268 in progress.
pulls.notes:
FIX for the dual-ENV_LOCK mutex bug that caused CI runs #27101158706 and #27102827375 to fail.

ROOT CAUSE: `mod tests` (line 567) and `mod probe_tests` (line 1228) each declared their own `static ENV_LOCK: Mutex<()>` on the same day (PR #11, 2026-06-07). The two locks did not coordinate. With `cargo test -- --test-threads=4` (CI default), cargo scheduled both modules' tests in parallel, and a `clear_all_config_env_vars()` in one module could wipe env vars another module's test had just set.

TWO INDEPENDENT CI FAILURES, SAME BUG:
  - Run #27101158706: probe_obscura_yaml_omits_binary_path saw a leaked STEALTH_CORE_OBSCURA_BINARY_PATH from a parallel test.
  - Run #27102827375: load_config_env_overrides_fingerprint found STEALTH_CORE_FINGERPRINT_ENABLED cleared by a parallel probe test.

FIX: One shared `pub(super) static ENV_LOCK` in new `#[cfg(test)] mod test_support` block. Both modules import via `use super::test_support::ENV_LOCK;`. The `use ...;` import also acts as a regression guard — any future re-introduction of a duplicate `static ENV_LOCK` will fail to compile.

VALIDATION: 20/20 local runs of `cargo test --lib -- --test-threads=4` pass (was 5/10 pre-fix). 55 lib tests pass (53 original + 2 new). All 3 Test Suite jobs in CI (ubuntu/macos/windows) pass.

NEW TESTS:
  - env_lock_serializes_parallel_env_var_writers: 8 workers × 50 iterations each, 50µs sleep in critical section, verifies env var persists.
  - env_lock_is_provided_by_test_support: compile-time regression guard against re-introducing a duplicate static.

POST-MERGE STATE (2026-06-08T06:10:56Z):
- Squash-merged into master as 5d20c16f
- PR branch fix/env-lock-deduplication auto-deleted on origin
- Local branch deleted with `git branch -D fix/env-lock-deduplication`
- Master HEAD: 5d20c16f
- 55/55 lib tests pass on master (cargo test --lib -- --test-threads=4)
- Triggered fresh CI on master (run 27119401268) via empty commit to validate post-merge stability.
- 0 open PRs, 0 open issues in stealth-core.

The two historical CI failures (#27101158706 and #27102827375) can no longer recur because:
  1. The dual-ENV_LOCK mutex bug is fixed.
  2. The `use super::test_support::ENV_LOCK;` import in both test submodules acts as a compile-time guard: any re-introduction of a duplicate `static ENV_LOCK` will fail to compile.
  3. The new `env_lock_serializes_parallel_env_var_writers` test stress-tests the lock with 8 workers × 50 iterations.
  4. The new `env_lock_is_provided_by_test_support` test verifies the invariant that the lock comes from the shared module.

- Tightened the doc to be honest: the test verifies the SHARED lock works, but the original cross-module bug is actually defended by the COMPILE-TIME GUARD (E0255 name collision on duplicate static declarations).

issues.title: Lifecycle log: engine overwrites manager's specific reason with generic 'firing_count=X, eff_ratio=Y'
actions_taken: Discovered 2026-06-12 during Phase C probes (finding C-F1)

Probe TestHardDemote::test_c7_testing_hard_demote_to_proposal failed: assertion on reason content failed because the reason was 'firing_count=100, eff_ratio=0.100' (engine's generic string) instead of the manager's 'auto: hard demote: ...' (specific)
Fixed in ae2b0ce: added LifecycleManager.last_reason_for(rule_id) returning the most recent transition's reason for the given rule

Fixed in 256d1a4: CorrelationEngine.evaluate_lifecycles now calls manager.last_reason_for() to preserve the specific reason in the SQLite lifecycle_log; falls back to the generic string if the manager didn't record a reason (defense-in-depth)
Probe re-run after fix: 3 hard-demote sub-probes pass, each recording the correct 'hard demote' or 'step demote' reason
issues.notes: Observability bug, not a functional bug. The audit trail was working but lossy. Before fix, the lifecycle_log could not distinguish hard-demote, step-demote, and auto-promote transitions — all rows looked identical. After fix, the distinction is preserved for forensics ('why did this rule transition?').

issues.title: Hard-demote silently rejected for VALIDATED rules: can_transition_to forbids VALIDATED->PROPOSAL
actions_taken: Discovered 2026-06-12 during Phase C probes (finding C-F2)

Probe TestHardDemote::test_c8_validated_hard_demote_overrides_step_demote failed: with VALIDATED rule + fires=100 + eff=0.10, lifecycle_log received 0 rows (manager returned None after can_transition_to rejected the override)

Root cause: LifecycleState.VALIDATED's allowed set was {PROMOTED, TESTING} — missing PROPOSAL. TESTING had {VALIDATED, PROPOSAL} and PROMOTED had {RETIRED, VALIDATED, PROPOSAL}; only VALIDATED was missing PROPOSAL.
Fixed in 66020eb: added PROPOSAL to VALIDATED's allowed set in LifecycleState.can_transition_to. Code comment documents why.
issues.notes: State-machine design bug. The hard-demote path was designed to override step-demote for any non-PROPOSAL state with bad stats, but the allowed map blocked the override for VALIDATED. The check at lifecycle.py:109-112 ('disallowed transition') returned None and logged a warning, so the bug was visible in logs but silent to callers. After fix, hard-demote works for all three non-terminal states (TESTING, VALIDATED, PROMOTED).

issues.title: [followup] Design: HermesRecallBackend.fetch() returns None for both 'not configured' and 'not found'
issues.next_action: Project owner to decide on sentinel classes vs is_configured property vs raise-on-misconfig.
actions_taken: Discovered 2026-06-12 during Phase B probes (issue #3, prior audit)
Probe TestAmbiguousNone::test_b3_caller_cannot_distinguish confirmed: caller gets None in both cases; only difference is log level (DEBUG vs WARNING) which caller can't see
issues.notes: API design change, not a bug fix. The current behavior (None means 'no result') is documented; changing the API is breaking. Three options proposed: (1) sentinel classes (NotConfigured, NotFound), (2) is_configured property, (3) raise on misconfiguration. Option 2 is least invasive.
